sections.heading: Periphrases with the gerund
sections.body:
- *ir* + gerund — gradual progress: *Poco a poco voy entendiendo.* (Little by little I'm starting to understand.) *La situación va mejorando.*
- *andar* + gerund — doing something repeatedly or aimlessly, often with a negative nuance: *Anda diciendo mentiras.* (He goes around telling lies.)
- *seguir / continuar* + gerund — to keep on: *Sigue lloviendo.*
- *llevar* + time + gerund — duration so far: *Llevo una hora esperando.*
- *acabar / terminar* + gerund — to end up doing: *Acabé comprando el más caro.* (I ended up buying the most expensive one.)

sections.heading: Periphrases with the infinitive
sections.body:
- *llegar a* + infinitive — to go as far as / manage to: *Llegó a ser ministra.* *No llegué a verlo.* (I didn't get to see it.)
- *deber de* + infinitive — probability: *Deben de ser las tres.* (It must be about three.) Compare *deber* + infinitive — obligation: *Debes estudiar.* (In speech the two are often mixed.)
- *venir a* + infinitive — approximately: *Viene a costar unos cien dólares.*
- *echar(se) a* + infinitive — to suddenly start: *Se echó a llorar.* *Echó a correr.*

sections.heading: Periphrases with the participle
sections.body:
- *llevar* + participle — accumulated result: *Llevo leídas cien páginas.* (I've read a hundred pages so far.)
- *tener* + participle — result, emphasizing completion or possession: *Tengo pensado viajar en junio.* (I've got it planned to travel in June.) *Ya tengo hechas las maletas.*
- *dar por* + participle — to consider as: *Doy por terminada la reunión.* (I declare the meeting over.)

examples: Little by little I'm starting to understand.
I ended up buying the most expensive one.
She went on to become a minister.
I didn't get to see it.
Viene a costar unos cien dólares.
It comes to about a hundred dollars.
I've read a hundred pages so far.
I'm planning to travel in June.
He ended up accepting the offer.
Los precios van subiendo cada año.
Prices keep going up every year.
